nodes.title: Decomposition of a power of x − α with exponents bounded by m/2 (BEG Lemma 5.1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree d and discriminant D_K, S a finite set of nonzero primes of 𝓞_K (BEG's S also contains the infinite places; s := #S + #(infinite places)), 𝓞_S the S-integers, f = a_0X^n + ⋯ + a_n ∈ 𝓞_S[X] of degree n ≥ 2 with D(f) ≠ 0, b ∈ 𝓞_S ∖ {0}, m ≥ 2, ĥ := ĥ(b, f) (coefficient-height-of-polynomial), and f = a_0(X − α_1)⋯(X − α_n) over a splitting field; L_i := K(α_i) and T_i the primes of L_i above S. For i = 1, 2 let h_{L_i}, R_{L_i} be the class number and regulator of L_i = K(α_i), t_i := #T_i (counting the infinite places), and η_{i1}, …, η_{i,t_i−1} a fundamental system of T_i-units with ∏_j h(η_ij) ≤ C_1 and max_j h(η_ij) ≤ C_1, C_1 := 1200(4n⁹s⁴)^{ns}·e^{2nd·ĥ}·|D_K|^n·(log* P_S)^{ns−1} (BEG (5.5)–(5.6), from fundamental-s-units-of-bounded-height). If x, y ∈ 𝓞_S, m ≥ 3, b·y^m = f(x) and y ≠ 0, then for i = 1, 2 there are γ_i, ξ_i ∈ L_i^× and integers b_{i1}, …, b_{i,t_i−1} with |b_ij| ≤ m/2 such that (x − α_i)^{h_{L_1}h_{L_2}} = η_{i1}^{b_{i1}}⋯η_{i,t_i−1}^{b_{i,t_i−1}}·γ_i·ξ_i^m and h(γ_i) ≤ C_2 := (2n³s)^{6ns}·|D_K|^{2n}·e^{4nd·ĥ}·(ĥ + log* P_S).
proofSteps: As in superelliptic-factor-coprimality, [x − α] = 𝔆_1𝔆_2^{−1}𝔄^m with integral 𝔆_1, 𝔆_2 ⊇ [a_0bD(f)] (using [1, α]^{−1} ⊇ [a_0]).
Raising to r := h_{L_1}h_{L_2} makes all three ideals principal (principal-generators-of-class-group-powers): (x − α)^r = γ_1γ_2^{−1}λ^m with [γ_k] ⊇ [a_0bD(f)]^r.

small-representative-modulo-s-unit-powers gives T-units ε_k with h(ε_kγ_k) ≤ (r/d_L)log N_T(a_0bD(f)) + cR_L + (h_L/d_L)log Q_T; write ε_2ε_1^{−1} = ζε^m∏_jη_j^{b_j} with |b_j| ≤ m/2 (reduce exponents modulo m in the fundamental system) and put γ := ζε_1γ_1/(ε_2γ_2), ξ := ελ.

nodes.title: Some place makes (x − α_1)/(x − α_2) very close to 1 (BEG (5.11)–(5.17))
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree d and discriminant D_K, S a finite set of nonzero primes of 𝓞_K (BEG's S also contains the infinite places; s := #S + #(infinite places)), 𝓞_S the S-integers, f = a_0X^n + ⋯ + a_n ∈ 𝓞_S[X] of degree n ≥ 2 with D(f) ≠ 0, b ∈ 𝓞_S ∖ {0}, m ≥ 2, ĥ := ĥ(b, f) (coefficient-height-of-polynomial), and f = a_0(X − α_1)⋯(X − α_n) over a splitting field; L_i := K(α_i) and T_i the primes of L_i above S. Let L := K(α_1, α_2), d_L := [L:ℚ], T the places of L above S, t := #T, r := h_{L_1}h_{L_2}, and let x, y ∈ 𝓞_S with b·y^m = f(x), m ≥ 3, y ≠ 0 not a root of unity. Put X := max_i h(x − α_i) and number the roots so that X = h(x − α_2). Then (a) m ≤ 2d(log 3d)³·(nX + 2ĥ); (b) if X > h(α_2) (which holds when X ≥ C_3), there is v_0 ∈ T with |1 − (x − α_1)/(x − α_2)|_{v_0} ≤ exp((n + 1)s(v_0)·log 2 + d_L·h(f) − X·d_L/t), where s(v_0) is 1, 2 or 0 for a real, complex or finite place; (c) if moreover X ≥ C_3 := (10n²s)^{37ns}·|D_K|^{6n}·P_S^{n²}·e^{11nd·ĥ}, then |1 − ((x − α_1)/(x − α_2))^r|_{v_0} ≤ exp(−X·d_L/(2t)). In particular, if X ≥ C₃ ≥ 2ĥ/n, then m ≤ 4nd(log 3d)³ X, equivalently X ≥ m/(4nd(log 3d)³). The factor n is required in this consequence of (a).
hypotheses: y ≠ 0, not a root of unity, m ≥ 3
proofSteps: (a): m·h(y) = h(f(x)/b) ≤ h(a_0) + h(b) + Σ_i h(x − α_i) ≤ 2ĥ + nX, and h(y) ≥ m(d) ≥ 1/(2d(log 3d)³) by voutier-height-lower-bound (y ∈ K has degree ≤ d).

(b): if |x − α_2|_v ≤ 1 for all v ∈ T then X ≤ h(α_2), excluded by hypothesis (and h(α_2) ≤ ĥ + (n + 1)log 2 by polynomial-height-versus-roots, so X ≥ C_3 suffices); otherwise choose v_0 ∈ T maximising |x − α_2|_v. Since x is an S-integer, X ≤ d_L^{−1}·log(|x − α_2|_{v_0}^t·∏_{v∉T}max(1, |α_2|_v)), so |x − α_2|_{v_0} is large, and 1 − (x − α_1)/(x − α_2) = (α_1 − α_2)/(x − α_2) with |α_1 − α_2|_{v_0}·∏_{v∉T}max(1, |α_2|_v)^{1/t} ≤ 2^{(n+1)s(v_0)}·exp(d_L·h(f)).

(c): for |1 − z|_v < 1 one has |1 − z^r|_v ≤ 2^{r·s(v)}|1 − z|_v (factor z^r − 1 = (z − 1)(z^{r−1} + ⋯ + 1)); with r bounded through class-number-and-regulator-bounds and X ≥ C_3 the error terms are absorbed, giving (5.17).

Since C₃ ≥ 2ĥ/n, (a) gives m ≤ 4nd(log 3d)³X. Keep this factor n in the height estimate for ξ₁/ξ₂; the stronger printed (5.12) does not follow from the preceding estimate. For part (c), use the correct compositum bounds d_L ≤ n(n−1)d and t ≤ n²s. After multiplying the error exponent by t/d_L, it is at most n²sH + 2n²s(r+n+1)log 2. The displayed C₃ dominates twice this quantity using the recorded bound for r, so the upper bound exp(−Xd_L/(2t)) follows. Do not use BEG’s root-field bounds nd, ns for this two-root compositum.
acceptance: For K = ℚ, S = ∅ the place v_0 is an archimedean place of L.
The hypothesis that y is not a root of unity is what bounds m by X in (a): for y = 1, f(x) = b has solutions for every m.
Part (c) needs r bounded independently of x, which the class number bounds provide.

nodes.title: Bérczes–Evertse–Győry's Schinzel–Tijdeman theorem over S-integers (Theorem 2.3, corrected constant)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree d and discriminant D_K, S a finite set of nonzero primes of 𝓞_K (BEG's S also contains the infinite places; s := #S + #(infinite places)), 𝓞_S the S-integers, f = a_0X^n + ⋯ + a_n ∈ 𝓞_S[X] of degree n ≥ 2 with D(f) ≠ 0, b ∈ 𝓞_S ∖ {0}, m ≥ 2, ĥ := ĥ(b, f) (coefficient-height-of-polynomial), and f = a_0(X − α_1)⋯(X − α_n) over a splitting field; L_i := K(α_i) and T_i the primes of L_i above S. If f(x) = b·y^m has a solution x, y ∈ 𝓞_S with y neither 0 nor a root of unity, then m is bounded by an explicit function of n, s, d, |D_K|, P_S and ĥ. BEG state m ≤ (10n²s)^{40ns}·|D_K|^{6n}·P_S^{n²}·e^{11nd·ĥ}; their estimate (5.19) omits the factor h_{L_1}h_{L_2} (sourceIssues), and restoring it and correcting the degree factor and infinite-place normalization, the calculation below gives m ≤ (10n²s)^{46ns}·|D_K|^{8n}·P_S^{n²}·e^{15nd·ĥ}. For K = ℚ, S = ∅ this reads m ≤ (10n²)^{46n}·e^{15n·ĥ}, which corrects the explicit bound recorded in DT.4/schinzel-tijdeman-theorem.
hypotheses: a solution with y ≠ 0 not a root of unity
proofSteps: Write H = ĥ, D = |D_K|, P = P_S, L = log*P, k = ns ≥ 2 and A = 10n²s ≥ 40. Put M = A^{46k}D^{8n}P^{n²}exp(15ndH). Assume m > M. The inequality m ≤ 2d(log(3d))³(nX+2H) gives X ≥ C₃ and hence X ≥ 2C₂. It also gives m ≤ 4nd(log(3d))³X. Indeed M/(4nd(log(3d))³) ≥ C₃ follows from d ≤ 2s and the factor A^{9k}D^{2n}exp(4ndH).

Set z = (x−α₁)/(x−α₂) and r = h_{L₁}h_{L₂}. The Baker form 1−z^r is nonzero: otherwise z is a root of unity, and z ≠ 1 since α₁ ≠ α₂. Then h(1−z) ≤ log 2 and x−α₂ = (α₂−α₁)/(1−z) imply X ≤ h(α₁)+h(α₂)+log 4 ≤ h(f)+(n+2)log 2 < C₃, a contradiction.

The decomposition gives h(ξ₁/ξ₂) ≤ 2(rX+C₂)/m + ½(t₁+t₂−2)C₁. Here r ≤ r₀ = (2n³s)^{4k}D^{2n}exp(4ndH). Since t_i ≤ ns and d ≤ 2s, h(ξ₁/ξ₂) ≤ [2r+1+8n²s²(log(6s))³C₁]X/m ≤ r·4^{k+2}C₁X/m. For the last comparison, log(6s)³ ≤ 6s², and 3+48n²s⁴ ≤ 4^{ns+2}; verify the latter at n=2,s=1 and increase n and s, using their exponential growth. This retains the n lost in printed (5.12).

Use m(d_L), with d_L = [K(α₁,α₂):ℚ], as the height floor in Proposition 3.10. The previous bound is also at least this floor (m(d_L) ≤ 1 and C₁ is large enough after X/m ≥ 1/(4nd(log(3d))³)). Each fundamental unit has h(η_ij) ≥ m(d_L), by its own field’s degree bound; therefore their product contributes at most C₁². Also max(h(γ₁/γ₂),m(d_L)) ≤ 2C₂. Thus Θ ≤ r C₄X/m, where C₄ = 2·10⁷(4^{10}n^{45}s^{18})^kD^{5n}exp(10ndH)(H+1)L^{3k−2}. Substitution of C₁,C₂ gives the stated coefficient: the remaining ratio is at most 2764.8/4^{3k} ≤ 1.

The Baker coefficient is at most C₅ = (32en²s)^{6k+3}, since d_L ≤ 2n²s and t₁+t₂ ≤ 2ns. At every place, N(v)/log N(v) ≤ 3P^{n(n−1)}: for an infinite place it is 2/log 2 < 3, while a finite place lies above S and has norm at most P^{[L:K]}. Comparison with the upper bound exp(−Xd_L/(2t)) gives m/log m ≤ 6n²s·r C₄C₅P^{n(n−1)}, using t ≤ n²s. This covers P = 1 as well as finite S.

Bound the numerical part of C₄ by A^{(45/2)k}, C₅ by A^{(8/5)(6k+3)}, and 6n²s by A. The first comparison follows from s^{18} ≤ s^{22.5} and 2·10⁷(4^{10}/10^{22.5})^k ≤ 1. For the second use 32e/10 < 40^{3/5}. Their exponent sum 32.1k+5.8 is at most 35k for k ≥ 2. Also (2n³s)^{4k} ≤ A^{6k}. Consequently m/log m ≤ Q := A^{41k}D^{7n}P^{n²−n}exp(14ndH)(H+1)L^{3k−2}.

To remove the remaining logarithmic factors, H+1 ≤ exp(ndH/2) and L^{3k−2} ≤ A^{3k}P^{n/2}. For P ≥ e, maximize u^{3k−2}exp(−nu/2) at u=2(3k−2)/n; its value is at most (6s)^{3k} ≤ A^{3k}. For 1 ≤ P ≤ e, L=1 makes the same estimate immediate. Hence M/Q ≥ A^{2k}D^nP^{n/2}exp(ndH/2).

Finally log M = 46k log A + 8n log D + n² log P + 15ndH. Each term is at most one quarter of A^{2k}D^nP^{n/2}exp(ndH/2): use 46k log A ≤ A^{2k}/4; 8n log D ≤ (8/e)D^n; n² log P ≤ (2n/e)P^{n/2}; and 15ndH ≤ (30/e)exp(ndH/2), with A ≥ 40,k ≥ 2. Therefore Q ≤ M/log M. Since t/log t is strictly increasing for t > e, m > M contradicts m/log m ≤ Q. This proves the corrected constant, conditional on the explicitly recorded source-input gaps, without invoking an unspecified final absorption.
acceptance: For K = ℚ, S = ∅, f = T² + 1, b = 1: every solution of X^p = Y² + 1 with X ≥ 2 has p ≤ (40)^{92} by the corrected bound (BEG's printed constant gives 40^{80}).
The hypothesis that y is not a root of unity is necessary: y = 1, f(x) = b is solvable for all m when f takes the value b.
The bound does not depend on the solution.

nodes.title: Effective Schinzel–Tijdeman theorem over S-integers, without analytic class-number inputs
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree d and discriminant D_K, S a finite set of nonzero primes of 𝓞_K (BEG's S also contains the infinite places; s := #S + #(infinite places)), 𝓞_S the S-integers, f = a_0X^n + ⋯ + a_n ∈ 𝓞_S[X] of degree n ≥ 2 with D(f) ≠ 0, b ∈ 𝓞_S ∖ {0}, m ≥ 2, ĥ := ĥ(b, f) (coefficient-height-of-polynomial), and f = a_0(X − α_1)⋯(X − α_n) over a splitting field; L_i := K(α_i) and T_i the primes of L_i above S. There is an explicitly computable number C(K, S, f, b), computable from K, S, f, b together with the class numbers h_{L_1}, h_{L_2} and fundamental systems of T_1- and T_2-units (all computable), such that f(x) = b·y^m with x, y ∈ 𝓞_S and y neither 0 nor a root of unity implies m ≤ C(K, S, f, b).
proofSteps: Repeat the structural ideal and unit-exponent reductions of Lemma 5.1 using computed class numbers and a chosen fundamental system, not its closed constants C₁,C₂. The generic covering bound gives a computable height bound for γ_i independent of m; the finitely many unit heights and the class-number product give the other fixed constants.

Use the elementary height estimate m h(y) ≤ nX+2ĥ and a positive computable lower cutoff for non-root-of-unity heights in the fixed fields. Voutier gives one such cutoff in every field involved, including auxiliary root fields of degree greater than one over a rational base; alternatively the coefficient-enumeration proof of Northcott below fixed multiplicative height 2 yields a field-specific positive minimum. That proof enumerates bounded-degree minimal polynomials with bounded integer coefficients; approximate the finitely many positive non-torsion logarithmic heights from below to obtain a certified positive cutoff.

At the large place use the Matveev comparison at infinity and the Yu 1994 adapter at finite places, with their actual constants. The same comparison gives m/log m bounded by a computable constant, and therefore a computable bound for m. Thus no analytic class-number bound or refined Győry–Yu closed constant is required. Over ℤ the logarithmic-form input is archimedean, alongside these height and unit-arithmetic inputs.
acceptance: For K = ℚ, S = ∅, f = T² − 1, b = 1 it bounds q in Y^q = X² − 1 (used by catalan-exponent-two-cases).
The constant is computable, not merely existent.
It is uniform in the solution.

nodes.title: Loher–Masser lower bound for a product of independent heights
nodes.statement: Let K have degree d and ω_K roots of unity. For n ≥ 1 and multiplicatively independent α₁,…,α_n ∈ Kˣ, 58(n!e^n/n^n)d^{n+1}log d · ∏h(α_i) ≥ ω_K if d ≥ 2. For d = 1 replace 58d^{n+1}log d by 17. Independence means that ∏α_i^{e_i} = 1 implies every integer e_i = 0.
hypotheses: n ≥ 1; the α_i are multiplicatively independent nonzero elements
proofSteps: Use Loher–Masser’s saturation lattice M of rational exponent vectors whose products are roots of unity times elements of K. Its covolume is 1/[M:ℤ^n]. Blichfeldt’s theorem applied to Σh(α_i)|x_i| < log H, whose volume is 2^n(log H)^n/(n!∏h(α_i)), produces enough distinct products in a shifted bounded-height set. Independence makes them distinct modulo the ω_K roots of unity.

Apply their shifted-height counting estimate (4.6), retaining both terms (d log d)(B′H^d+4CH^{2d}). Choose H = exp(n/(2d)); Lemma 5(e) gives B′/√e+4C < 58. The real-embedding estimate is stronger, and the rational case has counting bound 17H². Thus Theorem 3 yields ω_K[M:ℤ^n] ≤ 58(n!e^n/n^n)d^{n+1}log d∏h(α_i), or the stated rational variant. Drop the index, which is at least one, to obtain Győry–Yu Proposition 1. The shifted counting estimate, its numerical bound and the Blichfeldt/saturation argument remain a recorded gap; ordinary Northcott finiteness does not provide them.
acceptance: For n = 1 and K = ℚ, 17e·log 2 ≥ 2 is consistent with α = 2 and ω_ℚ = 2.
A root of unity cannot occur in an independent family, so the left-hand side is positive.
The d = 1 exception is necessary: retaining log d would give a zero left-hand side.
